rationale: Block 4 covers the LMN nature of poliovirus anterior horn cell destruction — the canonical trap is students confusing PPRP's flaccid LMN paralysis with UMN spasticity seen in CP.
Block 8 covers tendon transfers and arthrodesis — a critical exam trap is the minimum donor muscle grade required before transfer, and knowing triple arthrodesis must wait until skeletal maturity.
Block 9 covers specific deformity patterns — equinovarus and foot drop are the highest-yield patterns; knowing which muscles are paralysed predicts the deformity and directs the transfer choice.
Block 4 covers the UMN pathophysiology of CP — the LMN-vs-UMN distinction is a canonical examination trap, and spasticity/hypertonia must be distinguished from the flaccidity of PPRP.

Block 7 covers spasticity management including botulinum toxin — the critical trap is that botulinum is only appropriate for DYNAMIC (spastic) deformity, not for FIXED structural deformity where it has no role.
Block 10 directly contrasts LMN (PPRP) vs UMN (CP) — a dedicated comparison block, and the most likely place an examiner would anchor a comparison question.
